- **The first exception.** The group throws the exception of the first arm in the arms' order, and the exceptions of the other arms are dropped by `quietlyJoin`. The specification allows it; walk at four threads gave another arm's ('catching -3 -3 -3 0'). A test that asserts which arm's exception a group throws would differ between the paths.
- **Which calls count.** The analyzer adds a function's name when it reaches its declaration (`ParallelismAnalyzer.forFnDeclDoFirst`), so a call of a function declared later in the file than the caller is not compute intensive, and an `atomic do … end` that holds such a call is (it is a `Do`). REPORT.md's "calls of named functions written outside the prelude's files" is broader than that. The analyzer is not this rung's to change (fork P2).

## The failure-mode question

The rung turns no error into a value. Two quiet things: at one thread, or where the pool does not fork, an arm after the one that throws does not run (fork P1; the base did the same); and the exceptions of later arms are dropped once the first leaves the group. A `VirtualMachineError` still leaves loudly, without the joins.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# checks.sh RUN ROUND: the record-landing workflow's mechanical checks, after a write round (ROUND 1 or 2)
3	# or before the commits (ROUND final, which final.sh runs).
4	#
5	# RUN is the run's folder, with run.env (prepare.sh). In the worktree, the script resets FACTS.md,
6	# POSITIONS.md, their histories, the gap ledger and its history to AT, the commit that the worktree was made
7	# at; checks the POSITIONS lines that cut-only.txt names with words-subset.py, against the reset files; then
8	# applies the entries writer's file with record.py apply (record.apply, or for final the judge's final.apply)
9	# and its row lines with ledger-clarity/apply.py (rows.rewrite, or final.rewrite); then its new rows with
10	# ledger.py add (rows.add; for final, final.add if the judge wrote one, else rows.add). In rows.add each
11	# row line, `| ? | ...`, goes in the section that the nearest `## TITLE` line above it names, a title of
12	# `ledger.py sections`; a row with no such line above it is not added, and the summary says so (the
13	# coordinator files it). The routing writer's
14	# edits of PLAN, PLAN-history, the review queue, INDEX and other notes stay as they are. Then it runs every
15	# check on the worktree: record.py check --base AT; ledger.py check; ledger.py landing-check BASE;
16	# check-index.sh; plan-moves.py; queue-check.py; and the length of each changed entry, lengths.py.
17	# record.py writes each history block "by climb batch N landing workflow (Opus)", the tier of the agents that
18	# wrote the text. It writes RUN/mech-ROUND.md: one line per check, pass or fail, with the PLAN lines that
19	# plan-moves.py lists to look at and the entries over 600 that grew (lengths.py), then each check's command
20	# and output.
21	# Exit 0 when every check passes (the length table only informs), 1 otherwise. The record files stay as
22	# applied, so the worktree's git diff shows the round's whole change.
23	set -uo pipefail
24	here=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
25	RUN=${1:?usage: checks.sh RUN ROUND}; ROUND=${2:?round: 1, 2 or final}
26	# shellcheck disable=SC1091
27	. "$RUN/run.env"
28	tools="$WT/explorations/coordinator/tools"
29	rec=(python3 "$tools/record.py")
30	led=(python3 "$tools/ledger.py")
31	if [ "$ROUND" = final ]; then apply="$RUN/final.apply"; rows="$RUN/final.rewrite"; else apply="$RUN/record.apply"; rows="$RUN/rows.rewrite"; fi
32	adds="$RUN/rows.add"; [ "$ROUND" = final ] && [ -e "$RUN/final.add" ] && adds="$RUN/final.add"
33	out="$RUN/mech-$ROUND.md"
34	record_files=(explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md
35	  explorations/coordinator/FACTS-history.md explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS-history.md
36	  explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md)
37	mkdir -p "$WT/tmp"
38	body=$(mktemp -p "$WT/tmp" mech.XXXXXX); trap 'rm -f "$body"' EXIT
39	summary=()
40	bad=0
41	last=''
42	step() {   # step NAME MUST(1|0) CMD...: run CMD in the worktree, keep its output for the report (and in $last)
43	  local name=$1 must=$2; shift 2
44	  local o code
45	  o=$(cd "$WT" && "$@" 2>&1); code=$?; last=$o
46	  if [ "$code" = 0 ]; then summary+=("- $name: pass"); elif [ "$must" = 1 ]; then summary+=("- $name: FAIL (exit $code)"); bad=1; else summary+=("- $name: exit $code (information)"); fi
47	  { printf '## %s\n\n`%s`, exit %s.\n\n```\n' "$name" "$*" "$code"
48	    printf '%s\n' "$o" | head -c 12000
49	    [ "$(printf '%s' "$o" | wc -c)" -gt 12000 ] && printf '\n... (cut at 12000 characters)'
50	    printf '\n```\n\n'; } >> "$body"
51	}
52	
53	git -C "$WT" checkout "$AT" -- "${record_files[@]}"
54	summary+=("- reset: the six record files at $AT")
55	
56	if [ -s "$RUN/cut-only.txt" ]; then
57	  cut=$(mktemp -p "$WT/tmp" cut-only.XXXXXX)
58	  found=$(python3 - "$apply" "$RUN/cut-only.txt" "$cut" <<'PY'
59	import re, sys
60	want = set(re.findall(r'[FP]-\d+', open(sys.argv[2]).read()))
61	lines = [l for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if re.match(r'- ([FP]-\d+) ', l) and re.match(r'- ([FP]-\d+) ', l).group(1) in want]
62	open(sys.argv[3], 'w').write(''.join(lines))
63	print('%d of the %d entries that cut-only.txt names have a line in the apply file' % (len(lines), len(want)))
64	PY
65	)
66	  summary+=("- cut-only.txt: $found")
67	  step "words-subset.py, the cut-only lines ($(grep -oE '[FP]-[0-9]+' "$RUN/cut-only.txt" | paste -sd ' '))" 1 python3 "$here/../record-clarity/words-subset.py" "$cut" --root "$WT"
68	  rm -f "$cut"
69	else
70	  summary+=("- words-subset.py: no cut-only.txt, nothing to check")
71	fi
72	if [ -s "$apply" ]; then
73	  allp=$(mktemp -p "$WT/tmp" positions.XXXXXX); grep -E '^- P-[0-9]+ ' "$apply" > "$allp" || true
74	  [ -s "$allp" ] && step "words-subset.py, every POSITIONS line of $(basename "$apply")" 0 python3 "$here/../record-clarity/words-subset.py" "$allp" --root "$WT"
75	  rm -f "$allp"
76	  step "record.py apply $(basename "$apply")" 1 "${rec[@]}" apply "$apply" --by "climb batch $N landing workflow (Opus)"
77	else
78	  summary+=("- record.py apply: no $(basename "$apply"), no entry changed")
79	fi
80	if [ -s "$rows" ]; then
81	  d=$(mktemp -d -p "$WT/tmp" rows.XXXXXX); cp "$rows" "$d/final.rewrite"
82	  step "ledger-clarity/apply.py $(basename "$rows")" 1 python3 "$here/../ledger-clarity/apply.py" "$d" --root "$WT"
83	  rm -rf "$d"
84	else
85	  summary+=("- ledger-clarity/apply.py: no $(basename "$rows"), no row changed")
86	fi
87	if [ -s "$adds" ]; then
88	  d=$(mktemp -d -p "$WT/tmp" adds.XXXXXX)
89	  # one file per row line, row-K.txt, and d/list: K, a tab, its section ('' when no ## line is above it)
90	  python3 - "$adds" "$d" <<'PY'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# checks.sh RUN ROUND: the record-landing workflow's mechanical checks, after a write round (ROUND 1 or 2)
# or before the commits (ROUND final, which final.sh runs).
#
# RUN is the run's folder, with run.env (prepare.sh). In the worktree, the script resets FACTS.md,
# POSITIONS.md, their histories, the gap ledger and its history to AT, the commit that the worktree was made
# at; checks the POSITIONS lines that cut-only.txt names with words-subset.py, against the reset files; then
# applies the entries writer's file with record.py apply (record.apply, or for final the judge's final.apply)
# and its row lines with ledger-clarity/apply.py (rows.rewrite, or final.rewrite); then its new rows with
# ledger.py add (rows.add; for final, final.add if the judge wrote one, else rows.add). In rows.add each
# row line, `| ? | ...`, goes in the section that the nearest `## TITLE` line above it names, a title of
# `ledger.py sections`; a row with no such line above it is not added, and the summary says so (the
# coordinator files it). The routing writer's
# edits of PLAN, PLAN-history, the review queue, INDEX and other notes stay as they are. Then it runs every
# check on the worktree: record.py check --base AT; ledger.py check; ledger.py landing-check BASE;
# check-index.sh; plan-moves.py; queue-check.py; and the length of each changed entry, lengths.py.
# record.py writes each history block "by climb batch N landing workflow (Opus)", the tier of the agents that
# wrote the text. It writes RUN/mech-ROUND.md: one line per check, pass or fail, with the PLAN lines that
# plan-moves.py lists to look at and the entries over 600 that grew (lengths.py), then each check's command
# and output.
# Exit 0 when every check passes (the length table only informs), 1 otherwise. The record files stay as
# applied, so the worktree's git diff shows the round's whole change.
set -uo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
RUN=${1:?usage: checks.sh RUN ROUND}; ROUND=${2:?round: 1, 2 or final}
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$RUN/run.env"
tools="$WT/explorations/coordinator/tools"
rec=(python3 "$tools/record.py")
led=(python3 "$tools/ledger.py")
if [ "$ROUND" = final ]; then apply="$RUN/final.apply"; rows="$RUN/final.rewrite"; else apply="$RUN/record.apply"; rows="$RUN/rows.rewrite"; fi
adds="$RUN/rows.add"; [ "$ROUND" = final ] && [ -e "$RUN/final.add" ] && adds="$RUN/final.add"
out="$RUN/mech-$ROUND.md"
record_files=(explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md
  explorations/coordinator/FACTS-history.md explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS-history.md
  explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md)
mkdir -p "$WT/tmp"
body=$(mktemp -p "$WT/tmp" mech.XXXXXX); trap 'rm -f "$body"' EXIT
summary=()
bad=0
last=''
step() {   # step NAME MUST(1|0) CMD...: run CMD in the worktree, keep its output for the report (and in $last)
  local name=$1 must=$2; shift 2
  local o code
  o=$(cd "$WT" && "$@" 2>&1); code=$?; last=$o
  if [ "$code" = 0 ]; then summary+=("- $name: pass"); elif [ "$must" = 1 ]; then summary+=("- $name: FAIL (exit $code)"); bad=1; else summary+=("- $name: exit $code (information)"); fi
  { printf '## %s\n\n`%s`, exit %s.\n\n```\n' "$name" "$*" "$code"
    printf '%s\n' "$o" | head -c 12000
    [ "$(printf '%s' "$o" | wc -c)" -gt 12000 ] && printf '\n... (cut at 12000 characters)'
    printf '\n```\n\n'; } >> "$body"
}

git -C "$WT" checkout "$AT" -- "${record_files[@]}"
summary+=("- reset: the six record files at $AT")

if [ -s "$RUN/cut-only.txt" ]; then
  cut=$(mktemp -p "$WT/tmp" cut-only.XXXXXX)
  found=$(python3 - "$apply" "$RUN/cut-only.txt" "$cut" <<'PY'
import re, sys
want = set(re.findall(r'[FP]-\d+', open(sys.argv[2]).read()))
lines = [l for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if re.match(r'- ([FP]-\d+) ', l) and re.match(r'- ([FP]-\d+) ', l).group(1) in want]
open(sys.argv[3], 'w').write(''.join(lines))
print('%d of the %d entries that cut-only.txt names have a line in the apply file' % (len(lines), len(want)))
PY
)
  summary+=("- cut-only.txt: $found")
  step "words-subset.py, the cut-only lines ($(grep -oE '[FP]-[0-9]+' "$RUN/cut-only.txt" | paste -sd ' '))" 1 python3 "$here/../record-clarity/words-subset.py" "$cut" --root "$WT"
  rm -f "$cut"
else
  summary+=("- words-subset.py: no cut-only.txt, nothing to check")
fi
if [ -s "$apply" ]; then
  allp=$(mktemp -p "$WT/tmp" positions.XXXXXX); grep -E '^- P-[0-9]+ ' "$apply" > "$allp" || true
  [ -s "$allp" ] && step "words-subset.py, every POSITIONS line of $(basename "$apply")" 0 python3 "$here/../record-clarity/words-subset.py" "$allp" --root "$WT"
  rm -f "$allp"
  step "record.py apply $(basename "$apply")" 1 "${rec[@]}" apply "$apply" --by "climb batch $N landing workflow (Opus)"
else
  summary+=("- record.py apply: no $(basename "$apply"), no entry changed")
fi
if [ -s "$rows" ]; then
  d=$(mktemp -d -p "$WT/tmp" rows.XXXXXX); cp "$rows" "$d/final.rewrite"
  step "ledger-clarity/apply.py $(basename "$rows")" 1 python3 "$here/../ledger-clarity/apply.py" "$d" --root "$WT"
  rm -rf "$d"
else
  summary+=("- ledger-clarity/apply.py: no $(basename "$rows"), no row changed")
fi
if [ -s "$adds" ]; then
  d=$(mktemp -d -p "$WT/tmp" adds.XXXXXX)
  # one file per row line, row-K.txt, and d/list: K, a tab, its section ('' when no ## line is above it)
  python3 - "$adds" "$d" <<'PY'
import os, sys
sec, k, out = '', 0, []
for ln in open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'):
    t = ln.strip()
    if t.startswith('## '):
        sec = t[3:].strip()
    elif t.startswith('|'):
        k += 1
        open(os.path.join(sys.argv[2], 'row-%d.txt' % k), 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(t + '\n')
        out.append('%d\t%s' % (k, sec))
open(os.path.join(sys.argv[2], 'list'), 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(''.join(x + '\n' for x in out))
PY
  nosec=()
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r k sec; do
    if [ -z "$sec" ]; then nosec+=("$k"); continue; fi
    step "ledger.py add, row line $k of $(basename "$adds"), in \"$sec\"" 1 "${led[@]}" add "$d/row-$k.txt" --section "$sec"
    summary+=("  - $(printf '%s\n' "$last" | head -1)")
  done < "$d/list"
  [ ${#nosec[@]} -gt 0 ] && summary+=("- ledger.py add: not added, no \`## TITLE\` line above them in $(basename "$adds"): row line(s) ${nosec[*]}; file each with ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE")
  [ -s "$d/list" ] || summary+=("- ledger.py add: $(basename "$adds") holds no row line")
  rm -rf "$d"
else
  summary+=("- ledger.py add: no $(basename "$adds"), no row added")
fi
step "record.py check --base $AT" 1 "${rec[@]}" check --base "$AT"
step "ledger.py check" 1 "${led[@]}" check --summary
step "ledger.py landing-check $BASE" 1 "${led[@]}" landing-check "$BASE"
step "check-index.sh" 1 bash explorations/coordinator/check-index.sh
step "plan-moves.py" 1 python3 "$here/plan-moves.py" --root "$WT" --base "$AT"
look=$(printf '%s\n' "$last" | grep -c '^LOOK ' || true)
[ "${look:-0}" -gt 0 ] && summary+=("  - plan-moves.py lists $look PLAN lines to look at (its LOOK lines below)")
step "queue-check.py" 1 python3 "$here/queue-check.py" --root "$WT" --base "$AT"
step "lengths.py" 0 python3 "$here/lengths.py" --root "$WT" --base "$AT"
grew=$(printf '%s\n' "$last" | sed -n 's/^lengths: [0-9]* already over 600 grew: //p')
[ -n "$grew" ] && summary+=("  - lengths.py: already over 600, and grew: $grew")
step "git diff --stat $AT" 0 git diff --stat "$AT" -- explorations/

{ printf '<!-- The record-landing workflow'"'"'s mechanical checks, round %s, in the worktree %s at %s: one line per check, then each command with its output, written by checks.sh. -->\n\n# The mechanical checks, round %s\n\n' "$ROUND" "$WT" "$AT" "$ROUND"
  printf '%s\n' "${summary[@]}"
  printf '\n%s\n\n' "$([ $bad = 0 ] && echo 'Every check passes.' || echo 'A check fails: see its section below.')"
  cat "$body"; } > "$out"
printf '%s\n' "${summary[@]}"
echo "checks.sh: $out written; $([ $bad = 0 ] && echo 'every check passes' || echo 'a check fails')"
exit $bad

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""lengths.py --root WT --base AT: each changed entry's length before and after.

For each FACTS or POSITIONS entry whose line in the worktree WT differs from its line at AT, the commit
that the worktree was made at: its number, its characters at AT and now, the change, and whether it stands
over the record's 600, the size that record.py reports. An entry already over 600 at AT that grew is marked
"grew past 600": the judge holds it unless the clause that its change owes alone explains the growth
(judge.md). The last line names each such entry. Information only; exit 0.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('--root', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--base', required=True)
a = ap.parse_args()
D = 'explorations/coordinator/'
SIZE = 600


def entries(text):
    out = {}
    for l in text.split('\n'):
        m = re.match(r'- ([FP]-\d+) ', l)
        if m:
            out.setdefault(m.group(1), l)
    return out


rows, grew = [], []
for f in ('FACTS.md', 'POSITIONS.md'):
    old = entries(subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'show', '%s:%s' % (a.base, D + f)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
    with open(os.path.join(a.root, D + f), encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        new = entries(fh.read())
    for k in sorted(set(old) | set(new), key=lambda k: (k[0], int(k[2:]))):
        if old.get(k) != new.get(k):
            b, n = len(old.get(k, '')), len(new.get(k, ''))
            mark = ', grew past 600' if b > SIZE and n > b else ', over 600' if n > SIZE else ''
            if b > SIZE and n > b:
                grew.append('%s (%+d)' % (k, n - b))
            rows.append('- %s: %s to %s characters (%+d)%s' % (k, b or 'none', n or 'gone', n - b, mark))
print('lengths: %d entries changed' % len(rows))
print('\n'.join(rows))
print('lengths: %d already over 600 grew%s' % (len(grew), ': ' + ', '.join(grew) if grew else ''))

The $\morespecificeq$ relation is reflexive and antisymmetric but not
necessarily transitive.  It is possible, for example, for
three types, $T$, $U$ and $V$, each excluding the other two,
to have coercions from $T$ to $U$ and from $U$ to $V$.  In
this case, $T \morespecificeq U$ and $U \morespecificeq V$ but
$T \not\morespecificeq V$.

Notice that if two tuple types have a bijective correspondence
between their element types then the $\morespecificeq$ relationship between
the tuple types is equivalent to applying the $\morespecificeq$
relation elementwise.

We say that $T$ is \emph{more specific} than $U$, and write $T
\morespecific U$, if $T \morespecificeq U \logicand T \neq U$.

We extend the definitions of no less specific and more specific to
declarations.  We say that a declaration $\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{no less
specific} than a declaration $\f(\Qs)$ if $\Ps \morespecificeq \Qs$.
Similarly, we say that a declaration $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{no less
specific} than a declaration $\Qs_0.\f(\Qs)$ if $(\Ps_0, \Ps)
\morespecificeq (\Qs_0, \Qs)$.  A declaration $\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{more
specific} than a declaration $\f(\Qs)$ if $\Ps \morespecific \Qs$.
Similarly, a declaration $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{more specific} than
a declaration $\Qs_0.\f(\Qs)$ if $(\Ps_0, \Ps) \morespecific (\Qs_0,
